caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1846 of 2012
lawyer:
Shaheed Alam, Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner
Farooque Hossain, Advocate instructed by Abul Quasem, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondents
parties:
Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation and another ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Amena Khatun and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
3. The facts relevant for disposal of this Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal are that the present respondent No. 1 filed the above mentioned Civil Revision No. 1129 of 2004 before the High Court Division calling in question the order dated 24.02.2004 passed by the learned District Judge, Tangail in Money Execution Case No. 9 of 2000 rejecting the objection of the judgment-debtor (the respondent No. 1 herein) against the execution of ex-parte decree dated 28.10.1999 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 26 of 1998 for realization of loan of the House Building Finance Corporation. Rule was issued in that civil revision. During pendency of that rule, on 29.02.2012, the judgment-debtor-petitioner filed an application praying for disposal of that rule stating that she had already paid the loan amount. The High Court Division, in allowing that application, made some observations to the effect that according to section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation cannot claim any amount more than 3 times of the principal loan amount and as such since the House Building Finance Corporation took Tk. 28,87,000/- from the judgment-debtor-petitioner, which was more than 3 times of the amount taken as loan by the judgment-debtor-petitioner, House Building Finance Corporation would have to return the excess amount which, the High Court Division calculated as Tk. 4,48,000/-. The High Court Division disposed of the rule with a direction to the House Building Finance Corporation to return that excess money to the petitioner within 2 weeks from the date of receipt of that order. 

 5. We have heard Mr. Shaheed Alam, the learned Advocate for the leave-petitioners-who has admitted that the House Building Finance Corporation has already got the entire decreetal amount amounting to 28,87,000/- from the judgment-debtor-petitioner-respondent and now there is no amount due to him and that the House Building Finance Corporation has issued a certificate also to that effect. The leaned Advocate, however, has mode submissions that the observation of the High Court Division that section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is applicable in this case and as such the judgment-debtor-petitioner is entitled to get back the amount which is in excess of 3 times Limes of the principal loan amount-is wrong inasmuch as the House Building Finance Corporation filed the above mentioned Miscellaneous Case No. 26 of 1998 as per Article 27 of the House Building Finance Corporation Order, 1973 (P.O. 7 of 1973) for realization of loan along with interest accrued thereon in the court of the learned District Judge, Tangail and the learned District Judge, Tangail also disposed of that case as per that P.O. 7 of 1973 and in that case there was no scope for application of section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. The learned Advocate has argued that the observations of the High Court Division to the effect that according to section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 the judgment-debtor-petitioner is entitled to get back the excess amount is erroneous and illegal and the direction also made by the High Court Division to the House Building Finance Corporation to return 4,48,000/- to the judgment-debtor-petitioner has been illegal. 

 6. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate and gone through the impugned order of the High Court Division. We find substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the leave-petitioners. The observations made by the High Court Division in the impugned order to the effect that section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is applicable in this case and as such the decree-holder House Building Finance Corporation cannot get any amount more than 3 times of the principal loan amount from the judgment-debtor-petitioner is wrong. The present case for realization of loan was not filed before the Artha Rin Adalat as per provision of the Arthat Rin Adalat Ain 2003, rather it was filed before the learned District Judge as per Article 27 of the House Building Finance Corporation Order, 1973 (P.O. 7 of 1973) . In this case there is no scope for application of section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003.
